solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailor, stabbed, doubled over

blocks.note: jack is an old word for a sailor, as in jack tar
to knife someone is to stab them

explanation.surface: A sailor is stabbed in a brawl and doubles over in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To jackknife is to bend sharply at the middle, folding like a pocket knife closing.

clue.text: Support for limb motionless initially in seizure

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
one piece is placed inside the other, sitting in it

blocks.note: the first letter of motionless
an arrest is a seizure by the police

explanation.surface: A limb held rigid during a fit needs support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seizure' suggests a medical fit, but here it is the police sense of seizing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest is the part of a chair on which you lean your arm, so it holds up a limb.

clue.text: Bird of prey child has on a string

blocks.note: first meaning: a hawk-like raptor
second meaning: a toy flown in the wind on a line

explanation.surface: A child keeps a captive hawk tethered by a cord.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a small raptor and the paper toy flown on a line, which was named after the bird.

clue.text: By the sound of it, swallowed a delicious drink

indicators.note: the solver must judge how the words are spoken, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: to neck a drink is British slang for gulping it down

explanation.surface: Someone appears to have gulped down a tasty drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is informal British for drinking quickly, so 'necked a' is said just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods in myth, so any delicious drink can be called that.

clue.text: Briefly run up to a series of boats

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: water runs, or flows
till means up to, as in waiting till noon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dashes over to a line of moored boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet, a group of boats sailing together in a line.

clue.text: Bore strict training

blocks.note: first meaning: to make a hole through something
second meaning: rigorous repetitive instruction, as on a parade ground

explanation.surface: Strict training is a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for boring a hole and a noun for disciplined, repetitive exercises.

clue.text: Best seats here, but a thousand can't sit down?

definitions.note: a place description standing for the noun

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
those who cannot sit must stand

explanation.surface: The prime seating at a stadium, yet a crowd of a thousand is left standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandstand is the main covered stand at a sports ground, where the best seats are found.

clue.text: Shortly put down one chapter in colloquial speech

indicators.note: shortly means made short, so the last letter of the phrase's word is lost

blocks.note: to demote is to put down in rank
the Roman numeral for one
C is a standard abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: A soon-to-be-dropped chapter is written in everyday speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic is the ordinary language of the common people, as opposed to formal or literary forms.

clue.text: Remove restrictions from disc, safely reformatted

indicators.note: reformatting rearranges the contents into a new layout

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A computer disk is wiped and reformatted so it can be freely used.
explanation.definitionFit: To declassify a document is to lift the secrecy restrictions on who may see it.

clue.text: Basket maker more comfy out of cold

indicators.note: out of means without, so the following letter is taken away

blocks.note: cosier means more comfortable
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A basket weaver is snugger once out of the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a willow whose flexible twigs are woven into baskets, so it is the material that makes them.

clue.text: Prepare to swallow a red wine at the start

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, is a famous red
the first letter of wine

explanation.surface: Someone readies themselves to gulp a glass of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A red wine' reads as one phrase, but 'a red' is a communist, Che.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing is what you do to food to get it ready for swallowing.

clue.text: Set of bells in collar, moving

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift out of their places into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Bells on an animal's collar jingle as it moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned bells in a tower, played from a keyboard.

clue.text: Steal identity, an informal one

definitions.note: one stands for identity, so this means an informal name

blocks.note: nick is British slang for steal
a name is what identifies someone

explanation.surface: An identity thief uses a casual alias.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is a familiar, unofficial name used in place of someone's proper one.

clue.text: Get thanks when opening a can

indicators.note: something opening a container sits inside it, at its mouth

blocks.note: taken as written
ta is informal British for thanks
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone is thanked for opening a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is informal British for thanks; 'when opening' means it sits just inside the can.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain something is to get or achieve it.

clue.text: Son makes big strides skiing here

definitions.note: a place description standing for the noun

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A boy strides out confidently while skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers go down the slopes, the inclined runs of a ski resort.

clue.text: In large level area place a meal for all to see

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
taken as written
tea is an evening meal in British usage
U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a picnic in the open on a wide flat stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an expanse of high, flat ground.

clue.text: Specimen, small, more than adequate

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A lab specimen is small but plenty for the test.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a portion taken as an example of the whole, which is what a specimen is.

clue.text: Regular staff, one looking after cattle

blocks.note: stock as an adjective means standard or regular, as in a stock phrase
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A farm's permanent employees include a herdsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockman is a farm worker in charge of livestock, especially cattle.

clue.text: Toxic gas over region

blocks.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
a zone is an area or region

explanation.surface: A poisonous cloud hangs over the district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen that is poisonous to breathe at ground level.

clue.text: A convict returning for festival

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
an old lag is a British term for a convict

explanation.surface: A released prisoner comes home in time for the celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public celebration or entertainment.

clue.text: Secretly look up to find castle tower

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: to peek is to take a furtive look

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a glance upwards at a castle's tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest central tower of a medieval castle.

clue.text: Female at Hebridean isle?

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A woman visiting a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' simply sets the two pieces side by side; the whole clue also hints at a Scottish girl, as the name is especially popular in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a female first name of Scottish origin, fitting a woman from the Hebrides.

clue.text: Simulated pressure on nurse

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
re means on or concerning, as in business letters
to tend the sick is to nurse them

explanation.surface: A nurse is put under fake pressure in a training exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretend as an adjective, informally, means make-believe or not real, so simulated.

clue.text: Part of simple sum in school exam

blocks.note: first meaning: the start of an addition such as ... two
second meaning: the test taken at about age eleven in Britain to decide entry to grammar schools

explanation.surface: A child meets a basic addition question in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleven-plus is the British selection exam for grammar school, and literally the opening words of an addition.
